\section*{Summary}
JopeDime's program search can rank programs by a \emph{business objective}: a fitness function that reads what a program
costs to train and to serve as well as how accurate it is. A cost can be priced or imposed as a hard limit; a program that
breaks a limit is refused, never ranked. We ran 14 named case studies on real corpus datasets against the strongest
alternatives we could run on our hosts, all scored by the same product evaluator on the same rows: CatBoost, LightGBM,
XGBoost, scikit-learn HistGB, AutoGluon (best quality), the tabular foundation models TabPFN v2 (Prior Labs) and Kumo Tabular
(NVIDIA), and Ridge, random forest, extra trees and $k$-NN.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Online fare quoting under a latency budget (case 03).} Evolved programs answer one request in
\CaseThreeAextendedRes\,\textmu s (p99) at RMSE \num{\CaseThreeAextendedAcc}, level with the best library, XGBoost
(\num{\CaseThreeXGBAcc}). Served from Python, every library takes \CaseThreeLibPNinetyNineMin--\CaseThreeLibPNinetyNineMax\,\textmu s per call.
The one model that is more accurate, TabPFN v2 (\num{\CaseThreeTabAcc}), costs \CaseThreeTabMsRow\,ms per row even in batch.
\item \textbf{Auditable models on 1{,}142 features (case 09, no leakage flag).} Extended evolution finds programs of
\CaseNineXNodes{} nodes with RMSE \num{\CaseNineAextendedAcc}: \CaseNineVsHGB\% against the most accurate alternative,
HistGB (\num{\CaseNineHGBAcc}), and better than AutoGluon (\num{\CaseNineAGAcc}, \CaseNineAGMB\,MB). The holdout is only
\CaseNineHoldRows{} rows, so the test look matters most here.
\item \textbf{Hourly refits billed per CPU second (case 02).} Evolution seeded with library-equivalent programs scores
\num{\CaseTwoEObj} on the business objective, \CaseTwoEVsBest\% against the best alternative (XGBoost, \num{\CaseTwoBestFeasibleObj}),
at XGBoost's accuracy and a quarter of its training CPU.
\item \textbf{Retraining before gate closure (case 01), an instructive loss.} Under the 0.49\,s retrain limit our best arm
(\num{\CaseOneEAcc}) beats XGBoost by \CaseOneEVsXGB\% and CatBoost and AutoGluon cannot retrain in time, but TabPFN v2 is
more accurate still (\num{\CaseOneTabAcc}): an in-context model has no training to limit, and the objective did not price
its \CaseOneTabMsRow\,ms-per-row prediction.
\item \textbf{More generations improve the objective.} Chained (extended) evolution lowered the business KPI below the best program of
generation 0 in \EvoXImproved{} of \EvoXCases{} cases, by a median \EvoMedianXGain\% (Section~\ref{sec:evolution}).
\end{itemize}
Where an alternative wins we say so (case 07, an honest near-miss, and the leaderboard in Section~\ref{sec:leaderboard}).
Four datasets proved to leak their target; we claim nothing from them (Section~\ref{sec:notclaimed}).

\section{What was built}
A fitness specification is data (JSON), never code. It can now read \emph{resource variables}:
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}p{2.2cm}p{13.6cm}@{}}\toprule
measured & \texttt{fit\_seconds}, \texttt{fit\_cpu\_seconds}, \texttt{predict\_seconds}, \texttt{predict\_us\_per\_row}, \texttt{predict\_rows\_per\_second},
\texttt{row\_latency\_p50\_us}, \texttt{row\_latency\_p99\_us}, \texttt{fit\_peak\_heap\_bytes}, \texttt{predict\_peak\_heap\_bytes} \\
structural & \texttt{model\_bytes}, \texttt{program\_nodes}, \texttt{stage\_count}, \texttt{train\_rows}, \texttt{hold\_rows} (reproducible) \\\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
A variable can be a priced term (\texttt{\{"metric":"resource","name":...\}}), a leaf of a custom per-row expression, or a hard limit
(\texttt{\{"metric":"constrained",...,"limits":[...]\}}). The program search (\texttt{jope pipeline run -{}-fitness}) measures these
readings for every candidate and records them in \texttt{observations.json}; \texttt{verify-receipt -{}-evidence} re-derives the
champion from the recorded values. Measured readings depend on the host, so a search that ranks by them evaluates one
candidate at a time.

\section{How the studies were run}
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Arms} (one budget each: 96 evaluations or 600\,s; RNG seeds 7, 11, 13):
  \textbf{A} generation 0 seeded by our deep-learning policy (step-60000), ranked by the business objective;
  \textbf{B} random generation 0, same objective;
  \textbf{C}/\textbf{D} as A/B ranked by accuracy only;
  \textbf{E} generation 0 seeded with our grammar's equivalents of the XGBoost, LightGBM and scikit-learn defaults.
  \emph{Extended} runs chain 3 rounds (5 on the arm64 host) of up to 1000 evaluations or 600\,s each; each round restarts from
  the 11 best feasible programs found so far.
\item \textbf{Limits and prices} were calibrated before any main run, from a separate calibration run: a limit sits at the
median reading, so it binds for about half of the candidates.
\item \textbf{Fair comparison.} Alternatives fit on exactly the same rows and are scored by the same evaluator
(\texttt{jopedime fitness evaluate}). A Python-served one-row call is mostly call overhead, so for latency cases every library is
also credited with its amortized batch latency (a \emph{native-serving proxy}).
\item \textbf{Hosts.} \BriefHosts{} (identical Threadripper PRO 3995WX); all arms of a case ran on one host. The arm64 Mac xbabe4
(Linux container) ran only extended chains of a structure-priced case (09), whose objective does not depend on the hardware.
\end{itemize}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 03
\subsection{Case 03 --- online fare quoting under a latency budget}
\begin{question}Which fare model is most accurate while quoting a single trip within a p99 latency budget?
Data: \CaseThreeName{} (\CaseThreeRows{} rows, \CaseThreeFeatures{} features; selection holdout \CaseThreeHoldRows{} rows).
Objective: RMSE subject to \CaseThreeLimits\,\textmu s.\end{question}
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}\begin{axis}[xmode=log,casechart,xlabel={one-row prediction latency, p99 (\textmu s, log)},ylabel={RMSE (lower is better)}]
\oursplot{03}{\vlimit{8.4}{latency limit}}
\end{axis}\end{tikzpicture}\\[-2pt]
{\footnotesize\color{alt}\CaseThreeOffScale}
\end{center}
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lrrr@{}}\toprule
 & RMSE & p99 latency (\textmu s) & feasibility \\\midrule
\csname @@input\endcsname data/03-table.tex
\bottomrule\end{tabular}
\end{center}
\begin{center}\evochart{03}\\[-2pt]\begin{minipage}{0.95\linewidth}\evocaption\end{minipage}\end{center}
\begin{finding}
\begin{itemize}
\item The business objective returns programs at \CaseThreeAextendedRes\,\textmu s whose accuracy (\num{\CaseThreeAextendedAcc}) is level
with XGBoost (\num{\CaseThreeXGBAcc}), the most accurate library, and better than CatBoost, LightGBM and HistGB.
\item Ranked by accuracy alone, the search finds programs (\num{\CaseThreeCAcc}) that cost \CaseThreeCRes\,\textmu s per request,
about three orders of magnitude over budget. The objective makes that trade explicit.
\item The most accurate model measured, TabPFN v2 (\num{\CaseThreeTabAcc}), needs \CaseThreeTabMsRow\,ms per row even amortized over a
batch on CPU: no serving path brings it near 8.4\,\textmu s. AutoGluon is \CaseThreeAGBytesMB\,MB.
\end{itemize}
\end{finding}
\begin{caveat}
With the native-serving proxy the boosted libraries would meet the budget, and the contest becomes accuracy, where our extended
champions and XGBoost are at parity. Pickup time is one of 11 features and validation uses random folds (medium leakage risk).
\end{caveat}

Data: OpenML \CaseNineName{} (\CaseNineRows{} rows; cut-0 trains on \CaseNineTrainRows{} and selects on \CaseNineHoldRows).
Objective: RMSE/0.18 + 0.1 $\times$ program nodes/4 (structural, reproducible on any hardware).\end{question}
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}\begin{axis}[xmode=log,casechart,xlabel={model size (bytes, log; ours canonical JSON, libraries native)},ylabel={RMSE (lower is better)}]

\begin{tabular}{@{}lrrr@{}}\toprule

\begin{center}\evochart{09}\\[-2pt]\begin{minipage}{0.95\linewidth}\evocaption{} Extended chains here ran 5 rounds on the arm64 host.\end{minipage}\end{center}
\begin{finding}
\begin{itemize}
\item Extended evolution reaches RMSE \num{\CaseNineAextendedAcc} with programs of \CaseNineXNodes{} nodes and a median
\CaseNineXKB\,KB: \CaseNineVsHGB\% against HistGB (\num{\CaseNineHGBAcc}, \CaseNineHGBBytes\,KB), and ahead of CatBoost
(\num{\CaseNineCatAcc}) and AutoGluon (\num{\CaseNineAGAcc}, \CaseNineAGMB\,MB).
\item The business KPI kept improving with generations: the extended chains lowered it by a median \evogain{09}{X}\% from generation 0.
\end{itemize}

\begin{caveat}
The objective prices program structure, which library models do not have, so they are compared on RMSE only. The selection holdout is
\CaseNineHoldRows{} rows and the extended chains scored thousands of programs on it, so the validation figure is optimistic by construction
(selection bias). This case is decided by the test look.
\end{caveat}

\FloatBarrier
\subsection{Case 02 --- hourly refits billed per CPU second, and why every cost must be priced}
\begin{question}When every hourly refit is paid in compute, which program minimizes forecast error plus the CPU cost of refitting?
Objective: RMSE/$\sigma$ + 0.1 $\times$ fit CPU seconds / median (selection holdout \CaseTwoHoldRows{} rows).\end{question}
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}\begin{axis}[xmode=log,casechart,xlabel={training CPU time (s, log)},ylabel={RMSE (lower is better)}]
\oursplot{02}{}
\end{axis}\end{tikzpicture}\\[-2pt]
{\footnotesize\color{alt}\CaseTwoOffScale}
\end{center}
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lrrr@{}}\toprule
 & RMSE & fit CPU (s) & feasibility \\\midrule
\csname @@input\endcsname data/02-table.tex
\bottomrule\end{tabular}
\end{center}
\begin{center}\evochart{02}\\[-2pt]\begin{minipage}{0.95\linewidth}\evocaption\end{minipage}\end{center}
\begin{finding}
\begin{itemize}
\item Seeded with library-equivalent programs, evolution scores \num{\CaseTwoEObj} on the business objective against XGBoost's
\num{\CaseTwoBestFeasibleObj} (\CaseTwoEVsBest\%): the same accuracy (RMSE \num{\CaseTwoEAcc} vs \num{\CaseTwoXGBAcc}) at a median
\CaseTwoERes\,s of training CPU against \CaseTwoXGBCpu\,s. TabPFN v2 scores \num{\CaseTwoTabObj}.
\item The lesson: this objective priced \emph{only} training CPU, so one DL-seeded champion is a \CaseTwoBigModelMB\,MB model that
predicts slowly. The search was free to trade away a cost nobody priced. An objective is a contract: price every cost the business pays.
\end{itemize}
\end{finding}
\begin{caveat}Time-ordered data validated on random folds (high leakage risk). The CPU price comes from the calibration rule, not a tariff.\end{caveat}

\FloatBarrier
\subsection{Case 01 --- day-ahead price forecast retrained before gate closure (an instructive loss)}
\begin{question}Which program gives the best P90 day-ahead price forecast that can be retrained inside the window before gate closure?
Data: \CaseOneName{} (\CaseOneRows{} rows; selection holdout \CaseOneHoldRows). Objective: P90 pinball loss subject to \CaseOneLimits\,s.\end{question}
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}\begin{axis}[xmode=log,casechart,xlabel={training time (s, log)},ylabel={P90 pinball loss (lower is better)}]
\oursplot{01}{\vlimit{0.49}{retrain limit}}
\end{axis}\end{tikzpicture}\\[-2pt]
{\footnotesize\color{alt}\CaseOneOffScale}
\end{center}
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lrrr@{}}\toprule
 & P90 pinball & fit (s) & feasibility \\\midrule
\csname @@input\endcsname data/01-table.tex
\bottomrule\end{tabular}
\end{center}
\begin{center}\evochart{01}\\[-2pt]\begin{minipage}{0.95\linewidth}\evocaption\end{minipage}\end{center}
\begin{finding}
\begin{itemize}
\item Among tree models, evolution from library-equivalent seeds wins under the limit: \num{\CaseOneEAcc} against XGBoost's
\num{\CaseOneXGBAcc} (\CaseOneEVsXGB\%). CatBoost (\CaseOneCatFit\,s) and AutoGluon (\CaseOneAGFit\,s, \num{\CaseOneAGAcc}) cannot retrain in time.
\item TabPFN v2 is the best feasible model (\num{\CaseOneTabAcc}): its ``training'' only stores the context (\CaseOneTabFit\,s), and its cost
moves to prediction, \CaseOneTabMsRow\,ms per row on CPU. The objective limited training and priced nothing else, so the result is correct
as declared. If the business also bounds forecast time, the objective must say so: the case-02 lesson again.
\item Ranked by accuracy alone, our search drifts to programs that need \CaseOneCRes\,s to train (median).
\end{itemize}
\end{finding}
\begin{caveat}Time-ordered market data validated on random folds: this measures in-distribution fit, not forecasting under regime change.\end{caveat}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- not claimed
\section{What we do not claim}\label{sec:notclaimed}
A leakage audit (Ridge $R^2$, an ordinary least-squares refit and each dataset's column list) demoted four datasets; results on them are not evidence:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{05 (Survey of Consumer Finances).} The target is INCOME and its components (wages, business, interest, capital gains, retirement,
transfers) are features; Ridge reaches $R^2=0.993$.
\item \textbf{11 (bike sharing).} The target is \texttt{casual} + \texttt{registered}, and both are features.
\item \textbf{13 (Loan Default Prediction).} LightGBM reaches $R^2=0.9994$ and \texttt{id} is a feature, consistent with that competition's known leak.
\item \textbf{06 (ETF prices).} Random folds reward interpolation in time; on a chronological split every model's error rises about tenfold.
\end{itemize}
Other limits:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Selection bias.} Extended chains score thousands of programs on one holdout, so their validation figures are optimistic; only the test look settles them.
\item \textbf{Instruments.} Our memory reading is heap growth (counting allocator), the libraries' is process RSS growth; our model size is canonical JSON, theirs native.
\item \textbf{Foundation models} ran on CPU only. Kumo Tabular (size \emph{small}) has results on cases \KumoCases{}; it was out of memory or not applicable on the others.
TabPFN v2 has results on cases \TabPFNCases{} so far; the rest are still running.
\end{itemize}

\section*{Reproducing this brief}
